title: Checkpointing, incremental verification, and the projection snapshot
note: A checkpoint caches a verification RESULT. These mutations delete the checks that keep it from becoming a second source of truth: the anchor is re-hashed rather than trusted, an incremental report is forced to admit it is incremental, and a checkpoint that does not describe the log in front of it is refused rather than used. C28-C34 attack D-2026-30: the checkpoint FILE pinned a snapshot and nothing anchored the pin, so a rewritten file naming a forged snapshot restored a canonical record no history could produce -- while the log itself went on verifying perfectly, because the forgery was never in it. The claim is now also a checkpoint.state record under the hash chain, and these remove one part of that binding each.

mutations.name: C28_a_checkpoint_need_not_be_anchored_in_the_log

mutations.name: C29_the_anchored_digest_is_not_compared
mutations.rationale: a rewritten checkpoint file naming a forged snapshot is confirmed by a record that says something else, and the comparison that exists to catch it is gone

mutations.name: C31_an_anchor_for_any_position_vouches_for_any_checkpoint
mutations.rationale: an anchor for an EARLIER checkpoint is read as vouching for a later one, which is the check that asking 'is there an anchor anywhere' would fail

mutations.name: C32_the_claim_is_never_written_to_the_log
mutations.rationale: checkpoints go back to being files nothing in the log attests, so every later load has to take one on trust

mutations.name: C33_the_anchor_names_the_position_after_the_one_it_covers
mutations.rationale: the record claims to cover the record that announces it, and load_from's match on the position stops finding its anchor

mutations.name: E26_describes_degenerates_to_could_describe
mutations.rationale: D-2026-34: a checkpoint of a different log of similar length would describe this one, so prune would delete while the log is in doubt

mutations.name: E27_latest_usable_asks_the_weaker_question
mutations.rationale: D-2026-34: the backwards walk stops at a checkpoint that merely fits, leaving the one that describes the log unexamined below it

mutations.name: C34_the_torn_tail_tolerance_swallows_every_failure
mutations.find: if not report.ok and not report.torn_tail_only():
mutations.rationale: the D-2026-51 tolerance widened to accept ANY log that does not verify, so a checkpoint could be written past a real break -- the exact thing the refusal exists for

mutations.name: C35_torn_tail_only_stops_checking_for_other_problems
mutations.rationale: a torn tail ALONGSIDE a broken chain or a witness that outruns the log would report as torn-tail-only, so damage and truncation would become checkpointable
